glossary.upstream.text: The backend a proxy host or location forwards to, written as scheme, host and port. A stream host's equivalent is called the target and carries no scheme.

glossary.location.text: A path prefix inside a proxy host with its own upstream and extra policy. It is always at least as restrictive as the host it sits in.

glossary.middleware.text: One reusable policy object in a host's chain: auth, headers, guard, rate-limit, rewrite or bouncer. The chain order is fixed, not the order you attach them in.

glossary.access-list.text: The IP gate: ordered allow/deny rules over CIDRs plus optional GeoIP country rules, evaluated against the derived client IP.

glossary.identity-provider.text: An OIDC issuer, a trusted forward-auth proxy, or an auth-request outpost, plus its group-to-role mapping. It has no effect until an auth gate references it.

glossary.outpost.text: The external service an auth-request gate calls to decide allow or deny, such as an Authentik proxy outpost.

glossary.parked.text: A host that reserves a domain and answers a fixed status, 404 by default. It still terminates TLS; it simply proxies nothing.

glossary.maintenance.text: A host, or the whole edge, answering 503 with Retry-After instead of dialling the upstream. Domains, certificate and DNS records are kept.

glossary.ledger.text: The committed record of what gpm owns: config/dns-ledger.yaml for DNS records, config/access-list-sources.yaml for fetched feeds. It is what authorises a deletion.

glossary.reconcile.text: One full-state pass of a reconciler: recompute the desired set from the whole config, compare it with reality, and apply the difference as a single commit.

glossary.apex-target.text: The single CNAME target every DNS-sync-managed record points at. It is not an ownership marker: a hand-written record aimed here is still left alone.

page.overview.text: The landing view: what this instance is serving right now and what still needs attention.
bullets: Counts link straight to the list behind them.
The getting-started checklist tracks the first certificate, host and gate.
Certificate and discovery warnings surface here before they break traffic.
The upstream tile shows healthy vs unhealthy group members, so a backend outage is visible without opening each group.

page.proxyHosts.text: Every domain gpm terminates TLS for and reverse-proxies to a backend.
bullets: One domain belongs to at most one enabled host.
The certificate is chosen from the TLS handshake by domain, not picked per host.
Middlewares and access lists attach here and run in a fixed order.
A location narrows one path prefix to its own upstream and policy.

page.redirects.text: Domains that answer with a 3xx to another name instead of proxying anything.
bullets: Use them for retired names, vanity hostnames, and apex to www.
Preserve path appends the original request path to the target.
They still need a certificate covering the domain to redirect over HTTPS.

page.streams.text: Raw TCP and UDP forwarding for services that do not speak HTTP.
bullets: Each stream host owns a listen port of its own.
SNI matching lets several TCP hosts share one port.
Passthrough never decrypts; terminate needs a named certificate.
Only IP and geo rules apply at L4: a basic-auth list cannot be used.

page.parkedHosts.text: Domains that answer but serve nothing, so a name you own never falls through to another host.
bullets: The default answer is 404; any status code works.
They terminate TLS like any other host, so they need certificate coverage.
Useful for reserving names and for suppressing wildcard fall-through.

page.certificates.text: The TLS material gpm serves: ACME-issued certificates it renews itself, or files you supply.
bullets: ACME dns-01 is the only way to get a wildcard; http-01 needs port 80 reachable.
A host never picks a certificate: the handshake matches SNI against every certificate's domains.
State, expiry and the last error are read from the material itself, not from config.
Custom certificates are read from the certificate store on the gpm host.

page.clientCAs.text: The trust anchors that verify client certificates at the TLS handshake, plus optional revocation and signing keys.
bullets: A client CA verifies peers; a certificate identifies this server.
Add a signing key and gpm can issue client certificates and .p12 bundles itself.
A CRL is checked on every handshake; the policy decides what an unusable CRL means.
A host opts in under TLS, client certificates (mTLS).

page.identityProviders.text: Where gpm sends people to prove who they are, and how their groups map to roles.
bullets: Three types: OIDC, forward-auth headers, and an external auth-request outpost.
A provider does nothing on its own until an auth gate references it.
Only an OIDC provider can also sign in to this admin panel.
Role mapping turns provider groups into the roles required roles checks.

page.accessLists.text: Who may reach a host, by IP range or by country.
bullets: Rules are evaluated top-down and the first match wins.
The default action applies when no rule matches; deny is the safe default.
A source is a remote IP feed a rule can reference by name.
Geo rules need a GeoIP database loaded on the instance.

page.middleware.text: Reusable policy steps any host or location can pick up.
bullets: Six kinds: auth, headers, guard, rate-limit, rewrite and bouncer.
Chain order is fixed: rate limit, access list, bouncer, auth, guard, headers, rewrite, upstream.
The same auth block can be written inline on one host instead.
Deleting one is refused while a host still references it.

page.upstreamGroups.text: Several interchangeable backends behind one name, with health checks and a distribution policy.
bullets: A host references the group instead of a single upstream.
Weight applies to round-robin and least-connections only.
A failed connection is retried on another member; a sent request never is.
Sticky sessions pin a client to its member with a signed cookie.

page.dnsProviders.text: API credentials for the DNS zones gpm writes into.
bullets: Used for dns-01 ACME challenges and for published records under DNS sync.
Four providers authenticate with a single API token; rfc2136 and acme-dns do not.
Store every credential as an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder.
A masked credential reads *** and must be replaced before saving.

page.errorPages.text: Custom HTML for the errors gpm generates itself.
bullets: Covers dead upstreams, denials, rate limits and auth refusals.
The upstream's own error body passes through unless you list its status.
Templates come from a directory of <status>.html files, or inline JSON.
Any proxy host can override all of this in its own editor.

page.integrations.text: The outside systems gpm talks to on your behalf.
bullets: DNS sync publishes CNAMEs for hosts that opted in, and only deletes what its ledger says it created.
Kubernetes and Docker discovery derive hosts from annotated workloads.
Access-list sync keeps remote IP feeds current.
Webhooks and notifications push config and operational events outward.

page.apiTokens.text: Non-interactive bearer credentials for scripts and CI.
bullets: The secret is shown once and never stored: only its SHA-256 digest is committed.
Scopes limit what each token may read and write.
Write implies read on the same subject.
Token management, settings writes, restore and whole-config revert need full admin.

page.accessLogs.text: A live tail of requests the proxy served.
bullets: Entries carry the derived client IP, not the connection peer.
The filter matches host, path, method, status and client.
Logging is a runtime toggle and keeps nothing on disk here.

page.history.text: Every config change, as a git commit against the config repo.
bullets: Each save is one commit with the object kind and name in its message.
A single object can be reverted without touching the rest of the config.
Backup downloads the whole repo; restore replaces it.

page.settings.text: What this instance is, who may administer it, and how it answers.
bullets: General covers the instance name, panel URL, admin sign-in and client-IP trust.
Headers holds the fleet-wide response-header defaults and strip list.
Advanced holds PROXY protocol, the discovery label prefix, metrics and HA.
Operations holds the fleet maintenance switch and SSO session revocation.

common.name.text: The object's identity and its filename in the config repo. Lowercase alphanumeric plus - _ . and immutable once created.

common.displayName.text: A human label shown in the UI. It has no effect on routing and can be changed freely.

common.disabled.text: Keeps the object in config but excludes it from the running proxy. A disabled host releases its domains and withdraws its DNS records.

proxyHost.tags.text: Free-form labels for grouping and filtering in the host list. They have no effect on how the host is served.

proxyHost.maintenance.text: Serves a 503 maintenance page instead of proxying. The host keeps its domains, certificate and DNS records.

proxyHost.domains.text: The domain names this host answers for. At least one is required, and a domain belongs to at most one enabled host.

proxyHost.upstreamGroupRef.text: Names an upstream group to forward to instead of the single address below. The group brings its own health checks and failover policy.

proxyHost.upstream.scheme.text: How gpm talks to the backend: http or https. With https the upstream host is what SNI and certificate verification use.

proxyHost.upstream.host.text: The backend's address (an IP or a hostname gpm can resolve). Not the public domain clients ask for.

proxyHost.upstream.port.text: The port the backend listens on.

proxyHost.upstream.path.text: A base path prefixed to every request sent to this backend. Leave it empty to forward the path unchanged.

proxyHost.upstream.hostHeader.text: Which hostname the backend sees in the Host header: the name the client asked for (default), the upstream's own address, or a fixed value.

proxyHost.upstream.hostHeaderCustom.text: The exact hostname to send as the Host header. A hostname, optionally with a port.

proxyHost.robotsNoIndex.text: Sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on every response, asking search engines not to index this host.

proxyHost.timeouts.connectSeconds.text: How long gpm waits to open a connection to the backend. Blank keeps the shared pooled transport.

proxyHost.timeouts.readSeconds.text: How long gpm waits for the backend's first response byte. It does not cut off slow streaming or websocket bodies.

proxyHost.compression.enabled.text: Gzips eligible upstream responses, honouring the client's Accept-Encoding. Never applied to websocket upgrades or event streams.

proxyHost.compression.minBytes.text: Responses smaller than this are sent uncompressed, because compressing them costs more than it saves.

proxyHost.compression.types.text: The media types eligible for compression. Blank uses gpm's built-in text, JSON, JS, CSS, SVG and XML list.

proxyHost.errorPages.dir.text: A directory of html/template files named <status>.html, plus an optional default.html, relative to the certificate store.

proxyHost.errorPages.inline.text: Status code (or "default") mapped to HTML source, for pages you would rather keep in config than in a file.

proxyHost.errorPages.interceptUpstream.text: Status codes for which the backend's own error body is replaced too. Normally only gpm's own errors get the custom page.

proxyHost.securityHeaders.text: Per-header overrides of the fleet defaults for this host. A name listed here replaces the settings value and its scope; names not listed keep theirs.

proxyHost.stripResponseHeaders.text: Extra header names removed from proxied upstream responses on this host, on top of the fleet strip list. The two lists are unioned.

proxyHost.trustedProxies.mode.text: Whether this host inherits the fleet trusted-proxy list, trusts nobody, or replaces it with its own. A custom list replaces the fleet list, it never extends it.

proxyHost.trustedProxies.text: CIDRs or bare IPs whose X-Forwarded-For this host believes when deriving the client IP.

proxyHost.dns.lanDirect.text: Publishes this host's domains as local CNAMEs on the LAN resolver when Pi-hole DNS sync is configured.

proxyHost.dns.publicCname.text: Publishes this host's domains as records in the authoritative public zone when Cloudflare DNS sync is configured.

proxyHost.tls.minTLSVersion.text: The lowest TLS version this host negotiates. 1.3-only drops clients that cannot do TLS 1.3, such as older embedded devices.

proxyHost.tls.forceSSL.text: Redirects plain HTTP requests for these domains to HTTPS.

proxyHost.tls.hsts.enabled.text: Sends Strict-Transport-Security, telling browsers to reach these domains over HTTPS only.

proxyHost.tls.hsts.maxAge.text: How long, in seconds, a browser remembers the HTTPS-only instruction. One year (31536000) is the usual value.

proxyHost.tls.hsts.includeSubdomains.text: Extends the HTTPS-only instruction to every subdomain, including ones this host does not serve.

proxyHost.tls.hsts.preload.text: Asks browser vendors to hard-code these domains as HTTPS-only for every visitor. Removal takes months, so only enable it when every name is permanently HTTPS.

proxyHost.tls.clientAuth.text: Asks the client for a certificate during the TLS handshake and verifies it against a client CA.

proxyHost.tls.clientAuth.caRef.text: The client CA whose trust anchor (and CRL, if configured) verifies presented client certificates.

proxyHost.tls.clientAuth.mode.text: Whether a valid client certificate is required for the handshake, or merely optional so a certless client still reaches the chain.

proxyHost.tls.clientAuth.identityHeaders.text: Sends the verified certificate's identity upstream as request headers. These headers are always stripped from untrusted peers, so only gpm can assert them.
Adds X-Client-Cert-SAN with the certificate's subject alternative names.
Adds X-Client-Cert-Serial with the certificate's serial number.
Adds X-Client-Cert-Fingerprint with the certificate's fingerprint.
The header name carrying the certificate subject. Defaults to X-Client-Cert-Subject.

proxyHost.middlewares.text: The middleware objects attached to this host. Evaluation order is fixed whatever order you tick them in.

proxyHost.accessLists.text: The access lists that decide which client IPs may reach this host. Every attached list must allow the request.

proxyHost.auth.text: An auth gate written directly on this host instead of as a shared middleware. Same handler, same position in the chain.

proxyHost.rateLimit.text: A rate limit written directly on this host instead of as a shared middleware. Same handler, same position in the chain.

proxyHost.locations.path.text: The path prefix this override matches, starting with a slash.

proxyHost.locations.upstreamGroupRef.text: An upstream group serving this path only, instead of the host's own upstream.

proxyHost.locations.upstream.scheme.text: Scheme for this path's own backend. Blank falls back to the host's scheme.

proxyHost.locations.upstream.host.text: Address of this path's own backend. Blank falls back to the host's upstream host.

proxyHost.locations.upstream.port.text: Port of this path's own backend. Blank falls back to the host's upstream port.

proxyHost.locations.stripPrefix.text: Removes the location path from the request before it reaches the backend, so /app/foo arrives as /foo. Use it when the backend expects to live at the root.

proxyHost.locations.middlewares.text: Middlewares for this path only. Leave it empty and the host's chain applies here instead.

proxyHost.locations.accessLists.text: Access lists for this path only. Leave it empty and the host's lists apply here instead.

proxyHost.locations.auth.text: An auth gate for this path only. The host's own sign-in still applies on top of it.

proxyHost.locations.rateLimit.text: A rate limit for this path only. The host's own rate limit still applies on top of it.

redirectHost.domains.text: The domain names that answer with this redirect. At least one is required.

redirectHost.targetScheme.text: The scheme of the redirect target. Auto keeps whatever scheme the request arrived on.

redirectHost.targetDomain.text: The domain visitors are sent to.

redirectHost.statusCode.text: Which 3xx to answer with. 301 and 308 are permanent and get cached by browsers; 302 and 307 are temporary.

redirectHost.preservePath.text: Appends the original request path and query to the target instead of redirecting everything to the target root.

streamHost.listenPort.text: The port gpm listens on for this stream. Two stream hosts may share a port only when every one of them matches on SNI.

streamHost.protocol.text: Whether this stream forwards TCP, UDP, or both. TLS and SNI options are TCP only.

streamHost.target.host.text: The backend address the bytes are forwarded to.

streamHost.target.port.text: The backend port the bytes are forwarded to.

streamHost.tls.mode.text: Whether gpm reads the TLS handshake at all: passthrough routes by SNI without decrypting, terminate decrypts here and speaks plaintext to the backend.

streamHost.tls.sniMatch.text: Server names this host claims on a shared port, e.g. db.example.com or *.example.com. Leave it empty to take every connection on a port of your own.

streamHost.tls.certificateRef.text: The certificate presented in terminate mode. This is the one host kind where the named certificate is authoritative rather than chosen by SNI.

streamHost.accessLists.text: IP and geo lists evaluated on the client address before any backend is dialled. A list with basic-auth users cannot be used on a raw stream.

parkedHost.domains.text: The domain names this host reserves. They answer, but nothing is proxied.

parkedHost.statusCode.text: The status returned for every request to these domains. Default 404.

certificate.type.text: Whether gpm obtains this certificate over ACME and renews it itself, or reads files you supply.

certificate.domains.text: The names this certificate covers. Use *.example.com for a wildcard, which requires the dns-01 challenge.

certificate.acme.email.text: The contact address registered with the ACME account. The CA uses it for expiry and policy notices.

certificate.acme.directoryURL.text: The ACME directory to order from. Blank uses Let's Encrypt production.

certificate.acme.keyType.text: The key algorithm for the issued certificate. ECDSA is the default and is smaller and faster than RSA.

certificate.acme.challenge.text: How the CA verifies you control the domain. http-01 is validated on port 80; dns-01 writes a TXT record and is the only way to get a wildcard.

certificate.acme.dnsProvider.text: The DNS provider whose API writes the dns-01 challenge record. Required for dns-01 and rejected with http-01.

certificate.acme.eab.text: External Account Binding, required by CAs such as ZeroSSL and Google Public CA to tie an ACME account to yours.

certificate.acme.eab.kid.text: The key identifier the CA issued for external account binding.

certificate.acme.eab.hmacKey.text: The base64url HMAC key the CA issued alongside the key identifier. Use a ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder so no secret is committed.

certificate.custom.certFile.text: The full-chain PEM file, relative to the certificate store on the gpm host. There is no upload here; the file must already exist.

certificate.custom.keyFile.text: The private key PEM file, relative to the certificate store on the gpm host.

clientCA.caPEM.text: The CA certificate bundle presented client certificates are verified against. Public material only, never a private key.

clientCA.generate.commonName.text: The subject common name of the CA gpm generates. Blank uses the object's name.

clientCA.generate.days.text: How long the generated CA certificate stays valid. Ten years is the usual choice for an internal CA.

clientCA.generate.org.text: An optional organisation name written into the generated CA's subject.

clientCA.crlFile.text: A certificate revocation list, PEM or DER, relative to the certificate store. It is re-read when the file changes.

clientCA.crlPEM.text: An inline PEM revocation list, for a short list kept in git. It changes only on a config reload.

clientCA.crlPolicy.text: What happens when a configured CRL is missing, unparseable, foreign-signed or stale: refuse the handshake (default) or let it through.

clientCA.caKeyFile.text: The signing key for one certificate in the bundle, relative to the certificate store. Setting it lets this CA issue client certificates.

clientCA.caKeyPEM.text: The same signing key inline. It must be a ${FILE:...} or ${ENV:...} placeholder: a literal private key is refused at commit.

clientCA.expiryWarningDays.text: How far ahead a certificate issued by this CA is reported as expiring. Blank or 0 uses 30 days. Advisory only; nothing renews on its own.

clientCA.issue.commonName.text: The subject of the client certificate to mint, and the name of the downloaded file.

clientCA.issue.days.text: How long the issued client certificate stays valid.

clientCA.issue.password.text: The password protecting the downloaded .p12 bundle. At least 12 characters; it is not stored anywhere.

clientCA.issue.sans.text: Optional comma-separated subject alternative names. An IP becomes an IP SAN, a value containing @ an email SAN, anything else a DNS SAN.

clientCA.renew.password.text: The password protecting the renewed .p12 bundle. At least 12 characters.

clientCA.renew.days.text: How long the renewed certificate stays valid. It gets a new key and serial with the same subject, and does not revoke the old one.

dnsProvider.provider.text: Which DNS API gpm talks to. The four token providers authenticate with a single API token; rfc2136 and acme-dns take a typed form instead.

dnsProvider.config.text: The credential keys this provider needs. Store every secret as an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder so nothing is committed.

dnsProvider.config.server.text: The nameserver the dynamic UPDATE is sent to. Host, host:port, or [address]:port; the port defaults to 53.

dnsProvider.config.zone.text: The zone the UPDATE is addressed to, not the challenge name itself.

dnsProvider.config.tsigKeyName.text: Exactly the TSIG key name configured on the nameserver.

dnsProvider.config.tsigSecret.text: The base64 TSIG secret from tsig-keygen. Use an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder so it is not committed.

dnsProvider.config.tsigAlgorithm.text: The TSIG algorithm, which must match the key on the nameserver. hmac-md5 is not offered and is rejected.

dnsProvider.config.ttl.text: TTL in seconds of the challenge TXT record, between 1 and 86400.

dnsProvider.config.transport.text: Whether the UPDATE goes over TCP or UDP. UDP is retried over TCP when the reply is truncated.

dnsProvider.config.timeout.text: How long one exchange with the nameserver may take, as a Go duration such as 30s.

dnsProvider.config.baseURL.text: The API root of your acme-dns server. Must be an http or https URL.

dnsProvider.config.username.text: The username from the acme-dns /register response.

dnsProvider.config.password.text: The password from the acme-dns /register response. Use an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder.

dnsProvider.config.subdomain.text: The subdomain from the acme-dns /register response. This is what your zone's permanent CNAME points at.

identityProvider.type.text: How this provider asserts identity: an OIDC redirect flow, headers from a trusted proxy, or a subrequest to an external outpost.

identityProvider.oidc.issuerURL.text: The OIDC issuer URL. gpm reads its discovery document from here, so it must be reachable from the gpm host.

identityProvider.oidc.clientID.text: The client identifier registered for gpm at the provider.

identityProvider.oidc.clientSecret.text: The client secret for confidential clients. Use an ${ENV:...} placeholder; a masked secret reads *** and must be replaced to change it.

identityProvider.oidc.scopes.text: The scopes requested at sign-in. Blank asks for openid, profile, email and groups.

identityProvider.oidc.usePKCE.text: Uses PKCE for the authorization code exchange. Recommended, and it lets a public client run with no secret at all.

identityProvider.oidc.requireVerifiedEma.text: Refuses a sign-in whose token does not mark the email address as verified.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.trustedProx.text: Which peers may assert identity headers such as Remote-User. Required, and separate from the client-IP trusted proxies in Settings.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.userHeader.text: The header carrying the signed-in username.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.emailHeader.text: The header carrying the signed-in user's email address.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.nameHeader.text: The header carrying the signed-in user's display name.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.groupsHeade.text: The header carrying the user's group memberships, which role mapping reads.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.groupsDelim.text: The character separating group names in the groups header. Defaults to a comma.

identityProvider.forwardAuth.amrHeader.text: The header carrying the authentication methods the upstream proxy used.

identityProvider.authRequest.outpostURL.text: The base URL of the outpost gpm asks about each request.

identityProvider.authRequest.pathPrefix.text: The path prefix gpm proxies verbatim to the outpost for its sign-in, callback and sign-out endpoints.

identityProvider.authRequest.authPath.text: The endpoint gpm calls to authorize each request. It answers allow or deny.

identityProvider.authRequest.copyHeaders.text: Response headers copied from the outpost onto the upstream request when it allows the call.

identityProvider.roleMapping.groupsClaim.text: The token claim (or header field) holding the user's groups. Defaults to groups.

identityProvider.roleMapping.adminGroups.text: Groups whose members get the admin role: full read and write.

identityProvider.roleMapping.userGroups.text: Groups whose members get the user role: read-only in the admin panel.

identityProvider.roleMapping.defaultRole.text: The role for a signed-in identity that matches no listed group. Blank grants none.

middleware.type.text: What this middleware does. The chain order is fixed regardless of type: rate limit, access list, bouncer, auth, guard, headers, rewrite, then the upstream.

middleware.auth.identityProvider.text: Which identity provider people are sent to. Not used in client-cert or basic mode, where the certificate or the local credentials are the identity source.

middleware.auth.mode.text: How sign-in happens. Blank takes the mode from the identity provider's own type; set it explicitly when you rely on exempt networks.

middleware.auth.requiredRoles.text: Roles the signed-in identity must carry, mapped from provider groups. Not supported in auth-request or basic mode.

middleware.auth.allowFrom.text: CIDRs or bare IPs that skip this gate entirely, compared against the derived client IP. Allowed in auth-request, client-cert and basic modes only.

middleware.auth.clientCertRoles.text: Maps a client certificate subject (CN=ops,O=Corp, or its bare common name) to a role. Leave it empty to admit any verified certificate.

middleware.auth.basic.realm.text: The realm shown in the browser's password prompt. Printable ASCII, no quotes or backslashes.

middleware.auth.basic.users.text: The accepted credentials, at least one and at most 64. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt server-side and never stored or returned in plaintext.

middleware.auth.basic.users.username.text: The username, compared in full. It may not contain a colon or a line break.

middleware.auth.basic.users.password.text: The password for this user. It is hashed with bcrypt server-side; leave it blank on an existing user to keep the current one.

middleware.headers.setRequest.text: Headers added to the request before it reaches the backend.

middleware.headers.setResponse.text: Headers added to the response on its way back to the client.

middleware.headers.removeRequest.text: Header names stripped from the request before it reaches the backend.

middleware.headers.removeResponse.text: Header names stripped from the response wherever this middleware is attached. For edge-wide removal use the fleet strip list in Settings instead.

middleware.guard.triggers.text: The conditions that make this guard fire. A trigger matches when every field it sets matches; at least one trigger is required.

middleware.guard.triggers.paths.text: Request paths this trigger covers. Leave empty to match any path.

middleware.guard.triggers.methods.text: HTTP methods this trigger covers. Leave empty to match any method.

middleware.guard.triggers.queryEquals.text: Query parameters that must equal these values for the trigger to fire.

middleware.guard.denyStatus.text: The status returned when a trigger fires. Default 403.

middleware.guard.allowFrom.text: CIDRs exempt from this guard's deny, compared against the derived client IP.

middleware.rateLimit.form.text: Whether the limit is expressed as requests per window or as a plain rate per second. Only the selected side is saved.

middleware.rateLimit.requests.text: How many requests one client may make per window before it is throttled.

middleware.rateLimit.window.text: The window the request count applies to, as a Go duration such as 10s, 1m or 1h.

middleware.rateLimit.requestsPerSecond.text: The steady-state rate one client may sustain, in requests per second.

middleware.rateLimit.burst.text: How many requests may arrive at once above the steady rate before throttling starts. Blank uses the request count rounded up.

middleware.rateLimit.blockFor.text: Once a client exceeds the limit, it is refused for this long regardless of token refill. Fixed, not extended by repeat requests.

middleware.rateLimit.allowFrom.text: CIDRs or bare IPs that bypass the limit entirely.

middleware.bouncer.provider.text: Which kind of bouncer answers: a CrowdSec local API, or any HTTP endpoint you run.

middleware.bouncer.onError.text: What happens when the bouncer cannot be reached: admit the request (fail-open, the default) or refuse it (fail-closed).

middleware.bouncer.url.text: For crowdsec, the local API base URL. For http, the full endpoint gpm calls.

middleware.bouncer.apiKey.text: Sent as X-Api-Key. Required for crowdsec: register one with cscli bouncers add. Use an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder.

middleware.bouncer.timeout.text: How long one call to the bouncer may take before the on-error behaviour applies. Default 2s.

middleware.bouncer.cacheTTL.text: How long a verdict for one client IP is reused before asking again. Default 60s.

middleware.bouncer.cacheMaxEntries.text: How many client verdicts are cached at once. Default 10000.

middleware.bouncer.denyStatus.text: The status returned to a banned client. Default 403.

middleware.bouncer.denyWith.text: Whether a denial renders the configured error page or a plain minimal body.

middleware.bouncer.stream.text: CrowdSec only: pull the whole decision set once and then deltas, so each request is a local lookup with no call to the API.

middleware.rewrite.replacePath.text: Exact-match rules: the request path must equal the key, and is replaced by the value.

middleware.rewrite.prefixRules.text: Prefix rules, matched on a path-segment boundary so /reports never captures /reports-evil. The longest matching rule wins.

middleware.rewrite.regexRules.text: Regex rules, anchored at the start of the path. Use $1 in the replacement for a capture group.

middleware.rewrite.rule.from.text: The path or pattern this rule matches.

middleware.rewrite.rule.to.text: The path the match is replaced with before the request reaches the backend. A rewrite is never a redirect.

accessList.defaultAction.text: What happens when no rule matches. Deny is the default and the safe choice.

accessList.rules.text: Ordered allow and deny rules over the derived client IP. They are evaluated top-down and the first match wins.

accessList.rules.action.text: Whether a matching request is allowed or denied.

accessList.rules.match.text: Whether this rule matches a literal CIDR you type, or every network in a named source declared below.

accessList.rules.cidr.text: A CIDR or bare IP address this rule matches.

accessList.rules.source.text: A source declared below; the rule covers every network in that source's last fetched set.

accessList.rules.paths.text: Exact request paths this rule is limited to, comma-separated and each starting with a slash. Empty means every request.

accessList.rules.methods.text: Upper-case HTTP methods a path-scoped rule covers. Only valid alongside paths; blank means GET and HEAD.

accessList.sources.text: Remote IP feeds this list fetches and a rule can reference by name.

accessList.sources.name.text: The name a rule references this source by. Unique within the list.

accessList.sources.url.text: Absolute https URL of a plain-text IP feed. Plain http is refused.

accessList.sources.interval.text: How often the feed is re-fetched, as a Go duration. Blank means 24h; anything below 1h is refused.

accessList.sources.maxEntries.text: Cap on how many networks the feed may contribute. Blank or 0 means 10000.

accessList.geo.countryAllow.text: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country codes admitted. A non-empty allow list takes priority over the deny list.

accessList.geo.countryDeny.text: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country codes refused when no allow list is set.

accessList.geo.onUnknown.text: What to do with an IP the database has no country for, such as a private or reserved range.

upstreamGroup.upstreams.text: The interchangeable backends behind this group name, in order. Duplicates are rejected.

upstreamGroup.upstreams.scheme.text: How gpm talks to this member: http or https.

upstreamGroup.upstreams.host.text: This member's address (an IP or a resolvable hostname).

upstreamGroup.upstreams.port.text: The port this member listens on.

upstreamGroup.upstreams.weight.text: Relative share of traffic for round-robin and least-connections, 1 to 256. Failover and ip-hash ignore it.

upstreamGroup.policy.text: How requests are spread across members. Failover always prefers the first healthy member; unhealthy members drop to the end whatever the policy.

upstreamGroup.stickiness.ttl.text: Pins each client to its assigned member with a signed cookie for this long. Blank disables stickiness.

upstreamGroup.stickiness.cookie.text: The cookie name carrying the pinned member. Blank uses gpm-sticky-<group name>.

upstreamGroup.healthCheck.path.text: An HTTP path probed to decide whether a member is alive. Blank falls back to a plain TCP connect probe.

upstreamGroup.healthCheck.intervalSecond.text: How often each member is probed.

upstreamGroup.healthCheck.timeoutSeconds.text: How long one probe may take before it counts as a failure.

upstreamGroup.healthCheck.rise.text: How many consecutive successful probes return a member to the rotation.

upstreamGroup.healthCheck.fall.text: How many consecutive failed probes take a member out of the rotation.

apiToken.name.text: The token's identity, shown in logs and the token list. Immutable, lowercase alphanumeric with - _ and .

apiToken.expiresAt.text: The instant the token stops authenticating. Blank never expires.

apiToken.scopes.admin.text: Grants every endpoint, including token management, settings writes, restore, whole-config revert and the pprof endpoints.

apiToken.scopes.text: What this token may reach, per subject. Write implies read on the same subject.

settings.appName.text: The brand label shown in the sidebar, the browser title and the login page. Blank falls back to Go Proxy Manager.

settings.externalBaseURL.text: The canonical public URL of this admin panel. OIDC builds its redirect_uri from it, so admin sign-in fails until it matches what the provider has registered.

settings.adminAuth.localLoginEnabled.text: Keeps username and password login available as an anti-lockout path. It only grants access when a local admin user and bcrypt hash are also configured.

settings.adminAuth.providers.text: Which identity providers may sign in to this admin panel. Only OIDC providers can; forward-auth and auth-request gate proxied hosts, not the panel.

settings.adminAuth.ssoOnly.text: Disables local login entirely. There is no in-band break-glass door: recovering from a provider outage means redeploying with local login re-enabled.

settings.trustedProxies.text: CIDRs or bare IPs whose X-Forwarded-For gpm believes. Empty trusts nobody, which is correct when gpm faces the internet directly.

settings.tls.minVersion.text: The fleet-wide TLS floor every listener negotiates. A proxy host's own minimum TLS version overrides it, in either direction.

settings.securityHeaders.text: Fleet-default response headers, applied set-if-absent so an app's own header is never clobbered. Any proxy host can override one in its editor.

settings.securityHeaders.name.text: The response header name. Strict-Transport-Security is refused here; HSTS is a per-host TLS setting.

settings.securityHeaders.value.text: The header value sent when the response does not already carry this header.

settings.securityHeaders.scope.text: Which responses this header lands on: all, generated-only (denials, sign-in redirects, error pages) or proxied-only.

settings.stripResponseHeaders.text: Fleet-default header names removed from proxied upstream responses. Only what the upstream sent is touched, never a header gpm adds.

settings.proxyProtocol.enabled.text: Reads the real client address out of the HAProxy PROXY protocol header on the HTTP and TCP stream listeners, honoured only from the trusted peers below.

settings.proxyProtocol.trustedCIDRs.text: CIDRs or bare IPs of the load balancers whose PROXY header is believed. Required when enabled: there is no trust-everyone mode.

settings.proxyProtocol.timeout.text: How long a trusted peer has to deliver a complete PROXY header before the connection is closed. Blank is 5s, maximum 1m.

settings.ingressDiscovery.annotationPref.text: One prefix per deployment, naming every annotation and label Kubernetes and Docker discovery read and write. Blank uses the default.
Relabels hosts still carrying the old prefix during the next reconcile, in one commit. Leave it off and existing hosts keep the old labels.

settings.maintenance.enabled.text: Puts every proxy host into maintenance whatever its own switch says. Redirect, parked and stream hosts keep serving, and ACME http-01 still answers.

settings.maintenance.retryAfterSeconds.text: The Retry-After sent on every maintenance response, per-host ones included. Blank is 300s, maximum 24h.

settings.errorPages.dir.text: A directory of html/template files named <status>.html, plus an optional default.html, relative to the certificate store.

settings.errorPages.inline.text: Status code (or "default") mapped to HTML source, kept in config rather than in a file. Template vars: .Status .StatusText .Host .RequestID

settings.errorPages.interceptUpstream.text: Status codes for which the upstream's own error body is replaced too. By default only gpm's own errors get the custom page.

settings.dnsSync.pihole.enabled.text: Reconciles local CNAMEs on the LAN resolver for every proxy host that opted in.

settings.dnsSync.pihole.url.text: The Pi-hole base URL, absolute http or https, with no /api suffix.

settings.dnsSync.pihole.appPassword.text: The Pi-hole application password used to authenticate. Use an ${ENV:...} or ${FILE:...} placeholder so no secret is committed.

settings.dnsSync.pihole.apexTarget.text: The CNAME target every managed LAN record points at. It is not an ownership marker: hand-written records aimed here are left alone.

settings.dnsSync.cloudflare.enabled.text: Reconciles records in the authoritative public zone for every proxy host that opted in.

settings.dnsSync.cloudflare.dnsProviderR.text: Names an existing DNS provider entry whose API token is reused for zone writes.

settings.dnsSync.cloudflare.zoneName.text: The zone the managed records live in, e.g. example.com.

settings.dnsSync.cloudflare.apexTarget.text: The CNAME content every managed public record points at.

settings.dnsSync.cloudflare.proxied.text: Sets Cloudflare's orange-cloud flag on created records. Off means DNS only.

settings.ingressDiscovery.enabled.text: Polls the cluster for annotated Ingresses and reconciles them into managed proxy hosts. Only labelled hosts are ever written or removed.

settings.ingressDiscovery.apiURL.text: The Kubernetes API server URL. Leave it empty to use the in-cluster endpoint. Must be https.

settings.ingressDiscovery.tokenFile.text: Path to a read-only ServiceAccount token. It is re-read periodically, so a rotated token is picked up without a restart.

settings.ingressDiscovery.caFile.text: Path to the CA bundle that verifies the API server's certificate.

settings.ingressDiscovery.pollInterval.text: How often the cluster is polled, as a Go duration. Minimum 15s; empty means 1m.

settings.ingressDiscovery.namespace.text: Limits discovery to one namespace. Blank watches all of them.

settings.ingressDiscovery.labelSelector.text: An optional server-side label selector narrowing which Ingresses are listed. The opt-in annotation is still required.

settings.ingressDiscovery.allowedDomainS.text: Required. A discovered hostname must equal or end in one of these, so a cluster manifest cannot publish an arbitrary name at the edge.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.upstr.text: The ingress controller's address, since in-cluster Service DNS is not resolvable from outside. The controller routes by the Host header gpm forwards.
An upstream group instead of the single address, preferred when the ingress controller runs on more than one node. Mutually exclusive with the upstream above.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.tls.c.text: Required. Discovery never issues per-host certificates, so point this at a wildcard certificate that covers the allowed suffixes.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.tls.f.text: Redirects http to https on every derived host.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.robot.text: Sends X-Robots-Tag on every derived host.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.middl.text: Middlewares applied, in order, to every derived host.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.acces.text: Access lists applied to every derived host.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.timeo.text: Connect and read timeouts, in seconds, for derived hosts. Leave both blank for the shared pooled transport.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.tags.text: Tags applied to every derived host, for grouping in the host list.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.allow.text: Narrows the global suffix list for hosts derived from this template. It must be a subset; leave it empty to use the global list.

settings.ingressDiscovery.template.defau.text: The LAN-direct setting derived hosts get when the annotation is absent.
The public-CNAME setting derived hosts get when the annotation is absent.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profiles.text: Named alternative templates an Ingress may select by name. Every profile is selectable by every annotating Ingress, so only define ones any tenant may choose.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profiles.name.text: The name an Ingress selects this profile by, in the profile annotation.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profileSelecti.text: Whether the Ingress annotation may pick a profile at all. rules-only ignores it and lets the rules below decide.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profileRules.text: Operator-side routing from namespace and labels to a profile, with no say from the Ingress author. Evaluated in order; the first match wins.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profileRules.n.text: The namespace this rule matches. Blank matches any namespace.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profileRules.m.text: Comma-separated key=value labels the Ingress must carry. Blank matches any labels.

settings.ingressDiscovery.profileRules.p.text: The profile a matching Ingress gets, or template for the default block.

settings.dockerDiscovery.enabled.text: Derives proxy hosts from labelled Docker containers, using the same templates, profiles and label prefix as Kubernetes discovery.

settings.dockerDiscovery.socket.text: The Docker Engine unix socket, as an absolute path. It is ignored when a host URL is set.

settings.dockerDiscovery.host.text: An Engine endpoint used instead of the socket. A read-only socket proxy is the recommended shape.

settings.dockerDiscovery.pollInterval.text: Fallback loop interval, as a Go duration with a 15s minimum. Container events drive the normal case.

settings.dockerDiscovery.tlsCert.text: Absolute path to the TLS client certificate, for an https Engine endpoint. Set it together with the key.

settings.dockerDiscovery.tlsKey.text: Absolute path to the TLS client key. Set it together with the certificate.

settings.dockerDiscovery.tlsCA.text: Absolute path to the PEM bundle that verifies the Engine endpoint. There is no skip-verify option.

settings.dockerDiscovery.network.text: The Docker network whose per-container IP becomes the upstream address.

settings.dockerDiscovery.publishedHost.text: The address a published container port is reached on.

settings.dockerDiscovery.usePublishedPor.text: Forwards to the host-published port instead of the container IP. Use it when gpm runs on the Docker host rather than in a shared network.

settings.dockerDiscovery.includeStopped.text: Lists non-running containers too. A stopped container has no address, so its host is skipped and frozen rather than derived.

settings.dockerDiscovery.allowedDomainSu.text: Required. A derived hostname must equal one of these, or end in a dot plus one of them.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.tls.ce.text: Required when discovery is enabled. Point it at a certificate covering the allowed suffixes.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.tls.fo.text: Redirects http to https on every derived host.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.robots.text: Sends X-Robots-Tag on every derived host.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.timeou.text: Connect and read timeouts, in seconds, for derived hosts. Blank keeps the shared pooled transport.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.middle.text: Middlewares applied, in order, to every derived host.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.access.text: Access lists applied to every derived host.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.tags.text: Tags applied to every derived host, for grouping in the host list.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.allowe.text: Narrows the global suffix list for hosts derived from this template. It must be a subset of the list above.

settings.dockerDiscovery.template.defaul.text: The LAN-direct setting derived hosts get when the label is absent.
The public-CNAME setting derived hosts get when the label is absent.

settings.dockerDiscovery.profiles.text: Named alternative templates a container may select by label. Leave it empty to reuse the Kubernetes discovery profiles.

settings.dockerDiscovery.profiles.name.text: The name a container selects this profile by, in the profile label.

settings.accessListSync.enabled.text: Keeps access lists that declare a remote source up to date. Turning it off freezes every list at its last fetch.

settings.accessListSync.pollInterval.text: How often the loop asks whether any source is due, as a Go duration. Minimum 1m, default 15m; each source carries its own fetch interval.

settings.webhooks.text: Endpoints that receive a JSON event after every config change. Delivery is async and best-effort, so a slow endpoint never blocks a save.

settings.webhooks.name.text: The webhook's identifier, shown in the delivery status and logs.

settings.webhooks.url.text: The absolute URL each event is POSTed to.

settings.webhooks.secret.text: Sent as the X-GPM-Webhook-Secret header so the receiver can verify the call. Use an ${ENV:...} placeholder.

settings.webhooks.disabled.text: Keeps the webhook configured without firing it.

settings.notifications.expiringThreshold.text: How many days before expiry an ACME certificate joins the daily expiry digest. Default 14.

settings.notifications.targets.text: Where operational alerts are sent: ntfy, Discord, or a generic webhook.

settings.notifications.targets.name.text: The target's identifier, shown in logs and delivery status.

settings.notifications.targets.type.text: Which receiver this is, which decides the payload shape: plain text for ntfy, an embed for Discord, a JSON envelope for generic.

settings.notifications.targets.url.text: The absolute endpoint: an ntfy topic URL, a Discord webhook URL, or any endpoint for generic.

settings.notifications.targets.secret.text: An ntfy access token or a generic bearer token, sent as an Authorization header. Unused for Discord, where the webhook URL is itself the credential.

settings.notifications.targets.disabled.text: Keeps the target configured without firing it.

settings.notifications.targets.events.text: Which event kinds this target receives. Empty selects the default set, which is everything except config.changed.
